brief: A three-storey red-brick warehouse block with dormers and a stepped roofline, rows of white-framed windows, now shops and flats. One photo. Older than 1970: Petoskey's Gaslight District (the town's model) is a row of 1880-1910 brick commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the Petoskey Grocery Company building (1899), a four-storey brick wholesale warehouse with stepped-gable dormers, converted to lofts with new windows; beside a railroad crossing; new lawn strips and young trees
